title: Van der Waerden number W(2,4) = 35 (formalize-only)
flags: known-classical (Van der Waerden 1927; exact value W(2,4)=35 due to Chvátal 1979 computer-assisted proof); formalize-only — do NOT re-fund as novel

COMPUTE-HEAVY: lower bound needs a certified 34-colouring witness (offline search + Lean check, Ramsey-wave pattern); upper bound W(2,4)<=35 has no short hand proof — the published argument is a large case analysis. Budget cap mandatory.
target_statement_shape: theorem w24_le_35 : ∀ (c : Fin 4 → Prop-decision colouring of Fin 35 ...), ∃ a d, mono AP
(exact shape mirrors ProofLab/VanDerWaerden.lean: vdw_le_9 / vdw_gt_8 lifted from 3-AP to 4-AP over Fin 35 / Fin 34)
recommendation: Bench candidate. Direct vocabulary carry-over from closed van-der-waerden-w23: same TwoColouring/mono-AP predicates, just k=4 and N=35. The upper-bound half is the risk: native_decide-style exhaustive checking does NOT scale to 2^35 colourings, so W(2,4)<=35 requires either a smart hand case-analysis transcription or SAT-certificate import (DRAT not available in Lean without new infra). Feasibility shape = hand upper bound + certified lower witness (Ramsey-wave pattern), but the hand part is much heavier than R(3,5)'s degree count. Include only as bench if Director wants additive-combinatorics continuity; otherwise defer.

literature_pinning: STATEMENT.md must pin: (a) 4-term AP convention {a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d} with d>0; (b) W(2,4) least N such that every 2-colouring of Fin N has a monochromatic 4-AP; cite Chvátal, 'Some hard van der Waerden problems', Theoretical Computer Science (1979) for the value 35 and its computer-assisted nature — flag that the UPPER bound is computer-assisted in literature, so a zero-sorry Lean proof must either reproduce the case analysis or import a certificate.
notes: Lower witness: known 34-colourings exist in literature (e.g. via SAT archives); offline generation + decidable Lean check is the easy half
